shaders.name: Shaders: What a Surface Answers To
shaders.truth: A familiar form can be evaluated as a surface rule. Coordinates, material, light and viewpoint affect its appearance; mesh geometry, collision and retained state remain distinct constructions.
shaders.qfep_connection: Earlier coordinates, forms, arrays and fields return as choices inside a material. The learner locates where each choice changes an appearance, a body or a record. Re-evaluating from current inputs differs from updating retained state; the final hall supplies that connection before Cellular Automata.
shaders.formula: surface sample → form rule → material response; retained state requires a connected input
shaders.description: Six halls carry a familiar point and cube through a colour mask, coordinate repetition, bump and normal maps, vertex displacement, a composed material, and a field that retains its previous state. Each required reconstruction sits beside a larger museum encounter. Optional returns remain available without becoming prerequisites.
shaders.estimated_time: Not measured: museum visit and code reconstruction are separate activities.
learning_objectives: Construct a shared UV distance mask; compare hard and soft visible boundaries with fixed geometry and collision
Repeat and shift sampling coordinates; distinguish tile address, local coordinates and physical size
Compare flat shading, height-derived normals and an encoded normal map under light without changing silhouette
Use bounded layered noise to compare colour, vertex normals and displacement; explain subdivision and separate physical support
Compose repeated pigment, a view-dependent rim and emission on fixed bodies; distinguish visible brightness from illumination
Plant and retain field data; read old state, write next separately; distinguish model update, palette and receiver
content: Shader_01_Shaping: one circle rule on two square receivers; same point controls radius and edge
Shader_05_Patterns: same circle and point; repeat and shift the lookup; optional garden and saved-record returns
Shader_11_QueerRubber: same receivers, point and circle; compare flat, height and normal-map shading under light
Shader_09_FBM: same point and rigid cube; replace squares with a subdivided plane and keep collision separate
Shader_12_PinkExtravaganza: return to rigid point and cube; compose dots, rim and emission; investigate the surrounding room
Shader_10_ReactionDiffusion: point plants in retained field; GPU updates previous state; old unbound panel and frost remain comparisons
